title: Highest temperature in London on September 6?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance points to a daytime maximum of 26°C in London on September 6, with morning cloud and rain clearing to sunny intervals and light southerly winds. This aligns with ensemble model consensus favoring mild advection of warmer air under building high pressure, pushing temperatures 4–5°C above the 1991–2020 September 6 average high near 21°C. Limited model spread and stable steering patterns support the market's strong weighting toward 26°C (48.5%), while the modest probabilities on 25°C and 27°C reflect minor uncertainties in cloud timing and exact peak readings. Updated forecasts and any late adjustments to boundary-layer mixing will be the next key data points for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from Météo-France and European ensembles show Paris reaching a daily maximum of 28–30°C on September 6 under southeasterly flow advecting warmer air masses, combined with high pressure and limited cloud cover that supports strong daytime heating. These conditions exceed the 1991–2020 climatological average high of roughly 23°C, positioning 29°C as the modal outcome in trader pricing. Minor model spread around afternoon peak values and potential for increased cloudiness introduce uncertainty between 28°C and 30°C, while cooler or hotter extremes remain low-probability given current steering patterns and surface observations. Final resolution will hinge on official station readings once the diurnal cycle completes.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 36–37°C as the most probable range for Chongqing’s peak temperature on September 6, 2026, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes (53% at 37°C, 34% at 36°C).** Subtropical high pressure and mostly clear skies are expected to promote strong daytime insolation, while the city’s basin topography limits ventilation and sustains heat. Recent days have seen highs of 34–36°C under similar patterns, providing a baseline. Model spreads introduce modest uncertainty—some runs (e.g., AccuWeather) reach 40–41°C under drier, sunnier conditions, while others (Yr.no, Worldmeteo) cap at 36°C amid slightly higher moisture or cloud cover. Low precipitation risk and light southeast winds further support elevated readings, but any late-day increase in humidity or thin cloud could trim the maximum by 1–2°C. Official China Meteorological Administration observations tomorrow will resolve the market.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple sources, including local Chinese meteorological services and international models, indicate clear skies, light northeast to north winds, and stable high-pressure conditions over Qingdao for September 6, supporting daytime highs near 28–30°C. This aligns with a modest warm spell persisting from early September, where recent daily maxima reached 29–31°C under similar sunny patterns, though climatological September averages hover around 26°C. Model consensus shows minimal cloud cover and low precipitation risk, limiting upward spikes while allowing potential for brief afternoon peaks near 31°C depending on exact observation timing and urban heat effects. The market's emphasis on 31°C and 30°C reflects aggregated trader assessment of these stable atmospheric conditions and verification thresholds, with limited scope for deviations absent unexpected frontal changes.

Model consensus clusters around 74–76°F, aligning with the market’s leading 74–77°F bins that together exceed 80% implied probability. Final NWS observations tomorrow will resolve the market based on the official daily maximum.
